bull_bear.body: Display JV with HKC is already attracting automotive OEM interest; lighting exports to U.S./EU retailers are outside AOP and represent upside; negative working capital cycle (-8 days) is exceptional in EMS; specialty EMS roadmap is being built with a consulting giant and has concrete inorganic targets; server manufacturing JV is policy-driven with tax holiday advantage
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Dividend: the Board on 12 May 2026 recommended a final dividend of Rs. 10.00 per equity share of face value Rs. 2 each for FY2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing AGM.
- Lighting divestment realised a stated total consideration of Rs. 140.30 crores (Rs. 115.30 crores for the undertaking and Rs. 25.00 crores for the subsidiary shares, "based on registered valuer's report").
- The Company holds a 2.38% non-operating stake in Aditya Infotech Limited; the deck's "Reported" Q1 FY27 column "Includes fair value gain on stake 2.38% held by Dixon in Aditya Infotech Limited amounting to Rs 519 Cr in Q1 FY27", and the deck runs a parallel "Adjusted" set that excludes it.
- Employee equity: the NRC on 31 July 2026 approved a grant of 4,000 stock options under Dixon ESOP 2023, vesting "over a period of three years from the date of grant", exercisable within one year of last vesting, priced off the prior day's closing price on the higher-volume exchange with any discount capped at 15% of market price and a floor at face value.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Mobile: 32-33M units FY26 (ex-exports), flat volume guidance for FY27 (ex-Vivo), ASP up 12-15%; IT Hardware: INR4,000cr+ revenue target, SSD manufacturing from Q2, Inventec JV in Q3; Telecom: INR5,000cr FY26, target INR7,500-8,000cr, microwave radios exported; Home Appliances: 0.3M new units capacity in Tirupati, robotic vacuums and dishwashers in pipeline; Lighting: INR850cr FY26, target INR1,700cr, export orders secured from U.S./EU retailers; Consumer Electronics: mini-LED TVs and soundbar TVs launched, 375K sq.ft expansion for 2-door fridges; Specialty EMS: strategic roadmap with consulting firm, inorganic opportunities in aerospace/defense/medical identified
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Deck carries the standing brand line "Dixon - The brand behind brands" on every page, and the board's Annexure-A profile of promoter Mr. Sunil Vachani states the Company "has been adjudged as one of the leading Indian EMS by various trade journals and industry bodies".
- The Company reports as a single business: the CODM "examines the Company's performance on the basis of a single operating segment namely Electronics Goods; accordingly segment disclosure is not required" - although the Q1 FY27 earnings presentation's contents page separately lists a "Segment Performance - Revenue, Capital employed & ROCE" section (that slide is not present in the extracted text).
- Both top executives are being locked in for a further five years from 5 May 2027 to 4 May 2032: Mr. Sunil Vachani as Whole Time Director and Mr. Atul B. Lall as Managing Director, each subject to shareholder approval; the deck says Mr. Lall "has been leading Dixon Technologies (India) Limited since foundation and built it to its current leadership position in the EMS Industry".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [PLI dispute] A subsidiary has recognised PLI incentive income for revenues exceeding the prescribed annual ceiling on the basis that other eligible applicants in the same target segment "have not fully utilised their respective ceiling entitlements"; Rs. 1,110.06 crores "remains outstanding and receivable as at 30 June 2026, pending formal determination and disbursement by the Project Management Agency", against which a liability of Rs. 603.95 crores payable to its customer has been recognised. The auditor drew an emphasis of matter on it, with conclusion not modified.
- [PLI basis of recognition] Recognition rests on "management's assessment of the performance of other applicants, using publicly available information and internally available data" and on "independent legal advice, which confirms the subsidiary's eligibility for incentive upon achievement of the prescribed conditions under the Scheme" - i.e. on estimates of third-party behaviour rather than on a PMA determination.
- [Audit scope] The principal auditor "did not review the interim financial results of two subsidiaries included in the Statement, whose interim financial results reflect total revenues of Rs. 2,336.50 crores, total net profit after tax of Rs. 32.21 crores and total comprehensive income of Rs. 32.27 crores, for the quarter ended 30 June 2026", relying instead on other auditors' reports.
- [Gain on divestment - conflicting figures] The standalone notes state the gain on sale of the undertaking and subsidiary shares as "Rs. 21.88 crores and Rs. 24.99 crores respectively", while the consolidated notes state "Rs. 21.88 crores and Rs. 6.19 crores respectively" - the deck carries both readings.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: PLI expiry causing 50-70bps margin headwind; memory chip inflation increasing ASP and COGS; margin compression optically visible but per-unit EBITDA stable; margin expansion expected from FY28 via localized components (camera modules from H2FY27, displays from FY28)
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 15-17% YoY to INR56,000cr (ex-Vivo); margin: Slight pressure in FY27, 40-50bps expansion from FY28 via components; order inflow: IT hardware 3x, telecom to INR7,500-8,000cr, lighting to INR1,700cr; capex/commissioning: INR1,058cr spent in FY26; display JV (HKC) and Q Tech expansion to complete by Q4FY27; SSD line in Q2FY27; server JV in pipeline
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: IT hardware: 3x revenue growth expected; Telecom: robust demand from network infrastructure; Lighting: 2x revenue target; Camera modules: 190M units capacity; Display JV: trials in Q3, mass production Q4FY27; Smartphones: strong order book from U.S. brands and Ismartu exports
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Vivo smartphone JV (potential +20-22M units annually); PLI 2 export incentives (potential +4-5M units); server manufacturing JV (policy tailwinds); industrial EMS (aerospace/defense/medical) targeting INR3,000-4,000cr revenue; display module JV scaling to automotive and IT; Ismartu export expansion to Africa
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality
